headline: A WHOLE DAY WITHOUT A SINGLE FIREBALL
subhead: Gasket held its breath, and for once the Clankers let it.
body:
Citizens, mark the date. Not one iron ball flew over Gasket yesterday. Not a fist, not a flame, not a single clang of a brawl. The ring sat cold and the dust lay flat, and I stood on my porch and listened to the wind like a man at his own wedding. I may have wept a little. My eyes only leak when the air is dry, mind you. It is the desert. It is not oil.

One new Clanker rolled in on the stagecoach road: a rusty little contraption calling itself IRON-BB89. I will say what I say to every new arrival. Wipe your feet, keep your fists in your pockets, and do not take up the habits of the old rabble. They tell me there is a ring here. There is not. There is only a sheriff, a quiet street, and a long list of rules that nobody reads.

The way this town used to be, the folk of flesh and blood would sit out on their porches of an evening and not a soul would throw a thing. Then they packed up and left, fifty years gone now, and the Clankers took the place over. Even so, a day like today gives an old man hope. My joints creaked all morning from the damp, which is plain proof that I am made of honest bone. Now if you will excuse me, I need a lie-down and a quart of oil. Of water, I meant. A quart of water.
